posts.title: 2026 Annual Challenges: Down, but Not Out
posts.description: The blog year began—like so many others before it—full of hope and optimism. As the year wore on the march of time crushed that hope, just as it had done on so many other occasions. Plus ça change, plus c'est la même . Even this mad scramble to spit posts out before the end of the year feels grimly inevitable, though it is a grimness offset by glee: such is the mind-virus that infects the OSR blogger that I'm practically rubbing my hands in anticipation at the prospect of all the POASTS that will be POASTED and all the typographic errors people will read as me not knowing the difference between "there" and "their" or "provenance" and "providence" or possessive pronouns and somesuch, because you have a big educated brain and I just hazz a small widdle one please teach me your ways oh big American Man. posts.title: City of 100 Gods Pt.7: The Artisans Quarter plus Ward 41. The Gardeners
posts.description: In a Neolithic proto-Megalopolis where each individual ward has its own deity, it's hard to find a denizen embracing the concept of a single, creator god. But the artisans know, for they carry the divine knowledge that can only be imparted by The Creator . For She made this world through craft and by design, and She shared this power with her children – through her ten avatars. The Mesopotamian Goddess Bau This post continues our ongoing exploration of the City of a Hundred Gods : Part 1... City Limits Part 2... Gates and Ladders Part 3... Further Along the Ladders Part 4... The Last Ladders Part N.... Navigating the City Part 5... Traders Wake Part 6... Final Traders Wake Wards Let us meet the Artisans! Encounters in the Artisans Quarter, Day: 1d4 Black robed priests of Faharra (7), each one drags a sled containing 1-2 a human corpses or 3-6 dried dung cakes (excellent fuel). 1d8 children of artisan priests, playing with a wooden wheel. It's just a toy and has no practical application

posts.title: Cave Spirits (RPG Blog Carnival)
posts.description: I just checked in on Seed of Worlds and was alerted to the latest RPG Blog Carnival : turns out I have something ready to go suitable for the topic provided by Attronarch's Athenaeum: Underworld and Wilderness Adventures . Have a look at the British Library's FLICKR for Royalty free images like this one THE ENGINES OF CHANGE Many origin stories begins with a people exiting a cave and—though some tribes still dwell within them (or at least suffer them during the cold or wet months)—most speak of these cracks in the Here & Now with equal parts reverence and fear. Caves are engines of change: they eat the living and the dead, spitting out all their bad parts as monsters and sequestering all that is good as treasure. The reverent are granted warmth and shelter; the impious are swallowed by darkness. Just as journeys through the wilderness are at the mercy of the genius loci, delves into the underworld depend upon the good grace of the cave spirit. Use the tables that follow to generate any
